title: Rigveda 9.44: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.44: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.44 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 684v-685r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.44.1-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 684v
translation.original_text:
1pra ṇa̍ indo ma̱he tana̍ ū̱rmiṁ na bibhra̍d arṣasi | a̱bhi de̱vām̐ a̱yāsya̍ḥ ||
2ma̱tī ju̱ṣṭo dhi̱yā hi̱taḥ somo̍ hinve parā̱vati̍ | vipra̍sya̱ dhāra̍yā ka̱viḥ ||
3a̱yaṁ de̱veṣu̱ jāgṛ̍viḥ su̱ta e̍ti pa̱vitra̱ ā | somo̍ yāti̱ vica̍rṣaṇiḥ ||
4sa na̍ḥ pavasva vāja̱yuś ca̍krā̱ṇaś cāru̍m adhva̱ram | ba̱rhiṣmā̱m̐ ā vi̍vāsati ||
5sa no̱ bhagā̍ya vā̱yave̱ vipra̍vīraḥ sa̱dāvṛ̍dhaḥ | somo̍ de̱veṣv ā ya̍mat ||
translation.text:
1INDU, to us for this great rite, bearing as 'twere thy wave to Gods, Unwearied, thou art flowing forQh.
2Pleased with the hymn, impelled by prayer, Soma is hurried far away, The Wise One in the Singer's stream.,
3Watchful among the. gods, this juice advances to the cleansing sieve Soma, most active, travels on.
4Flow onward, seeking strength for us, embellishing the sacrifice: The priest with trimmed grass calleth thee.
5May Soma, ever bringing power to Bhaga and to Vâyu, Sage And Hero, lead us to the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 684v (numbered 1v by the scribe) (OPenn image 685, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.44.1 ‹pra naḥ indo iti›. Invocation (śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ hariḥ oṃ) and the anukramaṇī for aṣṭaka 7 on lines 1-5; 9.44.1 (pra naḥ indo iti) begins in line 5 after oṃ. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 685r (numbered 2r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.44.6 ‹vasuttaye kratu-vit gātuvit-tamaḥ vājam›. Verses 9.44.1-5 end on this page.

2matī | juṣṭaḥ | dhiyā | hitaḥ | somaḥ | hinve | parāvati | viprasya | dhārayā | kaviḥ
3ayam | deveṣu | jāgṛviḥ | sutaḥ | eti | pavitre | ā | somaḥ | yāti | vi-carṣaṇiḥ
4saḥ | naḥ | pavasva | vāja-yuḥ | cakrāṇaḥ | cārum | adhvaram | barhiṣmān | ā | vivāsati
5saḥ | naḥ | bhagāya | vāyave | vipra-vīraḥ | sadāvṛdhaḥ | somaḥ | deveṣu | ā | yamat

translation.original_ref: RV 9.44.6 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 1, varga 1); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 685r
translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>sa no̍ a̱dya vasu̍ttaye kratu̱vid gā̍tu̱vitta̍maḥ | vāja̍ṁ jeṣi̱ śravo̍ bṛ̱hat ||
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>So, to increase our wealth to-day, Inspirer, best of Furtherers, Win for us strength and high renown.
